Holographic Principle — Information on Boundaries

The holographic principle states that all information inside a region can be encoded on its boundary. It is inspired by the area scaling of black‑hole entropy and is realized precisely by AdS/CFT: a gravity theory in a bulk spacetime equals a non‑gravitational quantum field theory on the boundary. The Ryu–Takayanagi relation deepens this by tying boundary entanglement entropy to areas of minimal bulk surfaces, hinting that spacetime geometry itself may emerge from entanglement.

Flow: area law → holographic encoding → AdS/CFT realization → entanglement builds geometry.

Holography reframes memory as boundary encoding. Bulk geometry and dynamics correspond to patterns of quantum information (entanglement) on a lower‑dimensional boundary; geometry itself can be reconstructed from entanglement structure.

  • AdS–CFT Correspondence: Equivalence between a gravity theory in Anti‑de Sitter space and a conformal field theory on its boundary.
  • Ryu–Takayanagi Formula: Entanglement entropy of a boundary region ∝ area of a minimal surface in the bulk (geometric proxy for information).
  • Entanglement ↔ Connectivity: Proposed links between entanglement and spacetime connectivity (e.g., ER=EPR conjecture).
